ContentNode.title: Lab 4A : RF System and Non-linear Analysis [1.5hr]

LocaleContent.title: Lab Overview
LocaleContent.content: This lab walks you through RF system design, single-tone HB simulation, frequency and power sweeps, and amplifier distortion modeling, culminating in the simulation of a real PDK amplifier.

LocaleContent.title: First Time Using Hands-on Labs?
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​

Welcome! If this is your first time taking a lab, navigate to the Appendix in the Table of Contents to review the interface and features before proceeding. For returning users, feel free to start your lab by clicking next in the manual.

LocaleContent.title: Using non-ANSI US Keyboard?
LocaleContent.content: If you are using non-ANSI US Keyboard, please click the gear icon to turn on Fix non-ANSI US keyboard layouts option.

LocaleContent.title: Split Screen Mode
LocaleContent.content: If you would like to view the lab manual in new window or second device, click the 3 dots to Open in a new window or Open with another device.

LocaleContent.title: Lab Guidance
LocaleContent.content:
It will take about 1.5hr to complete all the modules in this lab.

Modules are not independent, so you must go through them all to complete this lab.

Lab Modules List :

  • Module 1 - RF system design
  • Module 2 - Harmonic Balance 1-Tone simulation
  • Module 3 - Examine the HB data
  • Module 4 - Variable power sweep setup
  • Module 5 - Display the swept power data
  • Module 6 - HB simulation of PDK amplifier system

LocaleContent.title: Let us Begin!
LocaleContent.content:
Click the shortcut icon for ADS on your screen, or use the Start > Programs command to find and start Advanced Designs System.

​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Lab 4A : RF System and Non-linear Analysis [1.5hr]
LocaleContent.content:
• Lab Overview
  • Lab Guidance

LocaleContent.title: Load workspace
LocaleContent.content:
1. Click Open Workspace
  2. Select  C:\ADS_Home\ADS101\Lab04\My_Sys_AMP_wrk

LocaleContent.title: a3_Sys_HB
LocaleContent.content:
The following parameters were set for the components:

  • P_1Tone source set Freq= 7.0 GHz.

  • Amplifier2 set S21=dbpolar (10,0).

  • LPF Butterworth filter set Fpass =7 GHz and Fstop = 8 GHz.

These are equation based behavioural models and provide approximate responses based on the settings you make. See the ADS documentation for further information.

LocaleContent.title: a3_Sys_HB
LocaleContent.content:
Open the schematic view of the cell a3_Sys_HB. 

​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Place wire label
LocaleContent.content:
1. Name the node between the P_1Tone source and Amplifier2 as “Vin".

  2. Name the node between the LPF_Butterworth and the R as “Vout".

LocaleContent.title: Module 1 - RF system design
LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • Load workspace
  • a3_Sys_HB
  • Place wire label

LocaleContent.title: Add HB controller
LocaleContent.content:
1. Select Simulation-HB palette (Harmonic Balance)
  2. Insert the HB controller.

LocaleContent.title: Set the HB frequency
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Set  Freq[1] = 7 GHz

This setting is important for HB: the source frequency and simulation analysis frequencies must match. If not, the simulation will run and report an error indicating the frequencies do not match. If they do match, all the tones (harmonics or inter-mods) will be correctly simulated.

LocaleContent.title: Run the simulation
LocaleContent.content:
Run the simulation.

Notice in the status window that the filter order is given as a warning. This can be ignored because the filter is behavioural. In general, ADS simulator warnings are easily understood or fixed. 

But if there is an Error, then it will not run and you will see the Error message.

LocaleContent.title: Module 2 - Harmonic Balance 1-Tone simulation
LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • Add HB controller
  • Harmonic Balance setup
  • Run the simulation

LocaleContent.title: Spectrum of V_out in dbm
LocaleContent.content:
Place your mouse pointer on the 7 GHz trace as shown here. 

​​​​​​​

The output power is about 7 dBm at 7 GHz which corresponds to the 0 dBm input power, plus 10 dB gain, minus the 3.01 dB attenuation at that frequency in the LPF.

LocaleContent.title: Spectrum of V_out in dbm
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. In the data display a3_sys_HB, Insert a rectangular plot 

  2. Add Vout​​​​​​​

  3. Select Spectrum in dBm.

  4. Click OK twice

LocaleContent.title: Mixing table
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Each frequency has an index number and also a mixing table which for 1-tone data is identical. But for intermodulation simulations, the mixing table makes it easy to select specific mixing terms out of the datasets.

Save and close the data display and the schematic.

LocaleContent.title: Mixing table
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Insert a List    
  2. Add Mix 
  3. Click OK

LocaleContent.title: Module 3 - Examine the HB data
LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • Spectrum of V_out in dbm
  • Mix table

LocaleContent.title: RF_pwr variable
LocaleContent.content:
Open the schematic view for cell a4_sys_psweep

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

There are two other changes to this schematic from the previous one. 

  • Amplifier2 has been assigned a 1 dB gain compression point at 22 dBm output power.

  • Fpass and Fstop of the behavioral LPF model have been increased.

Notice that the variable RF_pwr was added to the schematic. This variable is used to set the power of the P_1Tone source.​​​​​​​ ​​​​​​​RF_pwr is defined in dBm, but the simulator does not understand that unit, and the function dbmtow() is used to convert dBm to Watt.

LocaleContent.title: HB sweep setup
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Double-click on the HB controller. 
  2. Select the Sweep Tab.  

The variable RF_pwr will be swept from –30 dBm to 10 dBm in 1 dB steps.

LocaleContent.title: Run the simulation
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. Click on Simulate > Simulation Settings

  2. Check the flag Use cell name.

  3. Click Apply

  4. Click Simulate

LocaleContent.title: Module 4 - Variable power sweep setup
LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • RF_pwr variable
  • HB sweep setup
  • Run the simulation

ContentNode.title: Module 5 - Display the swept power data

LocaleContent.title: Gain equation
LocaleContent.content:
The data display a4_Sys_psweep will open once the simulation completes. 

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Notice there is already an equation for Gain on the data display. This equation is only correct when the input impedance of the amplifier and of the load is exactly 50 Ohms.​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Add Vout to the plot
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Insert a rectangular plot. ​​​​​​​
  2. Double-click Vout. 
  3. Select Fundamental Tone in dBm over all sweep values.
  4. Click OK

ContentNode.title: Change the Y-axis to Right Y Axis

LocaleContent.title: Change the Y-axis to Right Y Axis
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​
  1. Double-click on Gain on the right side under Traces (opens Trace Options dialog). 
  2. Select the Plot Axes tab, change the Y-axis to Right Y Axis.
  3. Click OK twice

LocaleContent.title: Add Gain to the plot
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Change the dataset to Equations
  2. Add Gain.

LocaleContent.title: Examine the data display
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  • Place a marker m1    
  • Place a line marker m2  on the Gain plot.  
  • Make sure that both m1 and m2 are at the same locations as shown in the plot.

The output power begins to flatten out as the amplifier goes into compression. It is easier to see the Gain compression on this plot than the power compression due to the scales used.

LocaleContent.title: lin_pwr equation
LocaleContent.content:
Notice there is an equation called lin_pwr defined on the data display. 

This equation was red (invalid) until you added marker m1 because the value of m1 is used in the equation and while it was missing the equation could not be evaluated.

Linear power is calculated as the input power plus the linear gain. This is why m1 must be at a power level at which the system is in the quasi-linear area of the response.

LocaleContent.title: Add lin_pwr to the plot
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Add lin_pwr to the plot.
  2. Click OK

LocaleContent.title: Examine the data display
LocaleContent.content:
Observe that it is now easier to see how the output power starts to compress. 

​​​​​​​

Save the data display.

LocaleContent.content:
This module contains the following lessons:

  • Add Vout to the plot
  • Add Gain to the plot

ContentNode.title: Module 6 - HB simulation of PDK amplifier system

LocaleContent.title: Deactivate amplifier
LocaleContent.content: Then Deactivate it. Now it will not be netlisted but is available for use later if needed.

LocaleContent.title: Move and disconnect amplifier
LocaleContent.content:
In the schematic window, press and hold the Ctrl key and then left-click and drag the Amplifier2 symbol away from the circuit (same as the menu command Edit > Move > Move & Disconnect). 

​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Add MeasEqn equation
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
  1. Type Meas, insert a MeasEqn component. 

  2. Edit the MeasEqn to:

    GAIN_db = dBm(Vout[::,1]) - 10*log( 0.5*real(Vin*conj(I_Probe1.i))[::,1]) - 30

  3. Save the design

The syntax [::,1] picks out the values of a computed quantity for all values of RFpwr but only at the fundamental frequency.

LocaleContent.title: It should look like this
LocaleContent.content: ​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Build amplifier system
LocaleContent.content:
​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

  1. In the Parts search field, type amp_ 

  2. Insert AMP_7GHz where Amplifer2 was before.

  1. Type i_p, ​​​​​​​insert an I_Probe symbol in front of the amplifier.

  2. Select the small wire segment between the pins of the I_Probe and delete it.

LocaleContent.title: Run the simulation
LocaleContent.content: Run the simulation.

LocaleContent.title: Add Gain_db to the plot
LocaleContent.content:
1. Add GAIN_db to the plot
  2. Choose the right y-axis under Trace Options.

LocaleContent.title: Examine the data display
LocaleContent.content:
The gains are slightly different because the amplifier’s input match is not exactly 50 Ohms.

​​​​​​​

LocaleContent.title: Close All
LocaleContent.content:
From the ADS Main window, use File > Close All and save your work.
